th 08/Dated: 10 June, 2025 I.A. No.6379 of 2025
1.

Heard Mr. Sushil Kumar Sharma, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Vishwanath Roy,
learned Special Public Prosecutor appearing for the State.

2. This interlocutory application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail during
pendency of this appeal.

3.  The appellant has been convicted for the offences under sections 341/34, 323/34, 504/34, 506/34 and 376(D) of Indian Penal Code and maximum sentence imposed upon him is R.I. for 25 years along with a fine of Rs.1,00,000/- for the offence punishable under section 376(D) of Indian Penal Code.
4. It has been alleged that the accused persons had committed rape upon the victim.
It has further been submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that allegations are general and omnibus in nature and the medical report does not support the factum of the case.

sentences.text: 5. Learned Spl.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

6. It appears from the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2 that the appellant is one of the accused persons,
who had committed rape upon P.W.1 and in the T.I. Parade, both P.W.1 and P.W. 2 have identified the appellant as the person who had indulged in committing rape upon the victim.
7. Regard being had to the aforesaid facts, we are not inclined to admit the appellant on bail.
The prayer for bail of the appellant is hereby rejected.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Pappu-Amar/-
